To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the development of human hunting technologies was driven by the need to overcome the limitations imposed by the human body and the environment, (2) the development of the technologies was accompanied by an expansion of causal cognition, (3) the expansion of the technologies was a key driver for the expansion of human causal cognition, and (4) the development of technologies and causal cognition was driven by the interplay between the human body and its environment.
the development of causal thinking in the hominin line is related to the development of force-dynamic reasoning.
(i) the development of hunting technologies is a window into the evolution of human causal cognition, and (ii) the evolution of causal cognition is a window into human technological evolution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution of causal cognition and how this evolution is related to the development of technology.
the evolution of causal cognition in hominins, with a focus on early hunting technologies.
the development of causal thought, which is a key element for the emergence of modern humans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
causal cognition and the development of force dynamics are two sides of the same coin.
there is a causal cognition continuum, with a gradual increase of causal complexity in the human lineage.
causal cognition, and force dynamics in particular, played a crucial role in the evolution of human hunting and technology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the evolution of causal cognition is an important element for the development of human cognition.
the evolution of hunting technologies is not a simple case of technological improvement but a complex interplay of technological, cognitive and cultural factors.
the development of hunting technology is not a matter of increasing efficiency, it is a matter of increasing causal cognition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to look at the whole package of hunting technologies to understand how they are used, and how this is connected to the cognitive capacities required to use these tools.
we can now better explain why and how the development of causal thinking and the invention of new technologies were intertwined in the hominin lineages.
causal cognition and technology are closely linked, and this relationship can be used to understand the evolution of causal cognition and the development of technology.
